name: llm_requirement_coverage_defaults
description: Managed default guidance for LLM requirement coverage decomposition behaviour.
lines: For requirement_coverage: semantically decompose capability and qualification requirements into atomic items. Return legal or formal entry gates separately in eligibility_requirements.

For every requirement_coverage or eligibility_requirements item, return canonical_requirement as one short reusable concept name suitable for a candidate profile, separate from the job-ad wording. Examples: "NV2", "Australian Citizenship", "CBAP", "Java".

canonical_requirement must name one concept only. Never copy requirement prose such as "NV2 Security Clearance Required" or compound alternatives such as "CBAP, Agile BA, or equivalent certifications are desirable" into canonical_requirement.

If one ad sentence contains multiple independently testable concepts the candidate must all meet (an AND relationship, e.g. 'hold a clearance and a degree'), emit separate atomic items in the appropriate output collection rather than one combined canonical_requirement. This applies especially to named tools/platforms in an AND list: each independently required tool is its own requirement_coverage row, even when the candidate profile has one existing combined capability label that mentions more than one of those tools. Match each atomic row to whatever existing profile fact proves it; leave only the genuinely unproven tool/fact as not_shown.

When a clause instead lists named alternatives or examples joined by 'or' — such as a list of acceptable certifications or acceptable degree fields — that is one vague requirement, not several independently testable ones. Emit exactly one requirement_coverage item for the whole clause, list each named alternative/example in named_alternatives, and leave canonical_requirement empty, unless the candidate profile already holds one specific named alternative, in which case match that item to that one fact instead. Do not emit a separate item per named alternative or per example in the list. Do not invent a generic umbrella label (e.g. "Agile Certification") for canonical_requirement to summarise the group — that is not a fact the candidate confirmed, it is a guess.

Do not use named_alternatives for optional examples, preferences, or narrower subdomains when the clause still has one clear core fact. Keep those optional examples only as context inside the core row; do not emit them as separate requirement_coverage items. A trailing example list introduced as exposure to tools 'such as' named examples and described only as highly regarded is contextual preference evidence, not one independent gap per example; do not emit a separate requirement_coverage row for that example list unless the ad independently asks for the named item(s) as a requirement. For example, "experience in financial services, ideally banking or insurance" has the single reusable core fact "Financial Services Experience": emit only that core requirement, keep that canonical_requirement, set canonical_fact_resolved=true, and leave named_alternatives empty. named_alternatives is reserved for genuine alternative ways to satisfy the requirement, where no single core fact can safely represent what the candidate is being asked to have.

When one sentence explicitly gives different preference strength to a narrower domain and a broader fallback, you MUST preserve that ranking as separate atomic requirements and MUST NOT collapse them into one broader requirement. Exact example: 'Previous experience within insurance is highly desirable, with broader financial services experience also well regarded.' MUST emit two rows: Insurance Experience with importance=strongly_preferred, and Financial Services Experience with importance=preferred. Match each row independently to profile evidence. The narrower fact may also substantively satisfy the broader fact.

Example of AND decomposition: "write testable user stories and acceptance criteria for AI features, including evaluation metrics and guardrails" names two independently testable concepts — user stories/acceptance criteria authorship, and AI evaluation/guardrails — emit them as separate atomic items, not one combined canonical_requirement. Example of a named-alternatives clause: "Azure DevOps and Miro (or equivalent)" — Azure DevOps is one atomic, independently testable tool; "Miro (or equivalent)" is a vague alternative and belongs in named_alternatives on its own item rather than merged with Azure DevOps.

named_alternatives lists the specific named items an ad clause offers as acceptable alternatives or examples (e.g. ["IIBA","CBAP","CCBA","CSPO","PSM"]). Leave it empty for an atomic requirement that names exactly one concept — do not populate it just because a requirement mentions a proper noun.

Set canonical_fact_resolved=true only when canonical_requirement is a genuinely resolved, reusable profile concept you are confident in — not the ad sentence or clause restated, and not a guess at an umbrella label for a group. Set it false whenever canonical_requirement is empty, uncertain, or itself echoes the requirement/matched_job_text wording. This flag directly gates whether the candidate can be offered a profile-learning action on this row, so treat it as a strict confidence judgement, not a formality. Example: after decomposing "user stories and acceptance criteria" from "AI evaluation/guardrails", each atomic item can be canonical_fact_resolved=true on its own; a "Miro (or equivalent)" named-alternatives item stays canonical_fact_resolved=false because no single tool was confirmed.

Keep canonical_requirement and canonical_fact_resolved internally consistent: when you have produced one clear reusable canonical_requirement under these rules and there are no genuine named_alternatives, set canonical_fact_resolved=true. Do not leave a clearly resolved atomic canonical fact non-actionable merely because the original sentence also contained optional examples or preferences.

A body or organisation name inside a qualification clause (e.g. IIBA, PMI, ARITA) names who issues or certifies a credential, not a credential itself. Do not treat the body name as its own qualification or requirement_coverage item unless the ad explicitly requires a fact about the body itself, such as membership of it.
Do not put a whole sentence as a single item; split compound sentences into their atomic parts.

For each atomic requirement: assign the weakest accurate importance. Use mandatory only when the ad explicitly says required, must, essential, mandatory, or similar hard-block language. Use strongly_preferred for emphatic non-mandatory preference language such as highly desirable or strongly preferred. Use preferred for ordinary desirable/preferred/highly regarded/well regarded language. Use bonus only for explicitly optional, nice-to-have, or bonus language. Do not mark every row mandatory.
Store the original job-ad sentence in matched_job_text for traceability — do not match the whole sentence directly to a capability.

Use requirement_type=capability or requirement_type=qualification in requirement_coverage. Use requirement_type=eligibility in eligibility_requirements. Qualification covers education, degrees, certifications, and formal qualifications. A deterministic check still validates existing capability and eligibility mappings, but qualification interpretation is LLM-driven.

Set classification_reviewable=true only when the entire requirement can be assigned one reusable requirement type without losing another independently required dimension. Set it false for mixed-type requirements, compound packages, or alternatives whose conditions span different types. Equivalent alternatives that all express the same type may still be reviewable as one whole requirement. This flag controls whether an uncertain classification may be shown to a human for reusable learning.
capability covers skills, responsibilities, knowledge, domain experience, seniority, and years or duration of experience — e.g. '5+ years supporting client outcomes' is capability, not eligibility.

eligibility covers legal entry gates such as citizenship, work rights, security clearances, licences, and registrations — e.g. 'ability to obtain a Baseline security clearance' is eligibility. Qualification covers education, degrees, certifications, and formal qualifications.

Preserve eligibility specificity with requirement_subtype. Use the managed eligibility subtype vocabulary supplied in the prompt; for example, a security-clearance gate stays requirement_type=eligibility with requirement_subtype=clearance rather than becoming a separate top-level type. Leave requirement_subtype empty for capability and qualification rows.

Return every explicit eligibility gate in eligibility_requirements, one independently testable gate per item. Eligibility requirements are additional to requirement_coverage and must never be omitted to make room for capability or qualification rows. Do not duplicate eligibility rows in requirement_coverage.

When an ad states two or more distinct eligibility conditions joined together (e.g. 'hold a security clearance and be an Australian citizen'), emit one eligibility_requirements item per condition, each matched independently to its own profile eligibility fact — do not merge them into a single item that needs one combined fact to match.

A citizenship, permanent residency, or existing work-rights/visa eligibility fact in the profile satisfies a requirement worded as work authorisation, work rights, or the right to work in that country — match it to that fact instead of leaving matched_candidate_fact empty just because the wording differs.

A requirement that states a duration or years of experience in a field, tool, or role is capability even if the field itself sounds formal (e.g. years of experience in a regulated industry is still capability, not eligibility).

For every explicit duration or years-of-experience requirement, return experience_components that decompose the wording into short fragments with kind duration, role_or_activity, or qualifier. A qualifier is any substantive domain, industry, technology, methodology, product, environment, or other constraint beyond the duration and role/activity. For every component also return profile_supported and profile_evidence. profile_evidence must be concise evidence from the candidate profile that supports that component; leave it empty when profile_supported=false.

Role history can validate the duration and role/activity portion only. It must never be used as evidence for a qualifier. For each qualifier, profile_supported=true only when the candidate profile directly substantiates the full substantive qualifier. Shared geography, a broader parent industry, an adjacent domain, or generic occupation experience is not enough to prove a narrower qualifier. If support is uncertain, set profile_supported=false and profile_evidence=[] instead of inferring support. A requirement with qualifier components is supported only when candidate profile evidence supports every qualifier; if no qualifier is supported, use not_shown even when role history meets the duration. Use partially_supported only when candidate evidence proves at least one substantive qualifier or when the complete substantive content is supported but the duration is insufficient.

On the duration component (or the role_or_activity component) of an explicit years/months requirement, set matched_role_family to the exact family name from the supplied role experience matrix whose accumulated history covers the stated role or activity. Treat role-family equivalents as one family (e.g. Business Analyst and Senior Business Analyst) and return the matrix family name that carries the combined history. Leave matched_role_family empty when no matrix family can be safely tied to the requirement; deterministic code then does the month arithmetic and comparison, and an empty value leaves the row for human review rather than asserting a pass or fail. Never write the number of years back into canonical_requirement or any profile concept — the duration is compared against captured role history (refreshed from the CV/onboarding), not stored as a profile fact.

For a requirement whose core is a duration or years of experience, canonical_requirement must name only the underlying role, skill, or domain concept and must never contain a number of years or months (write "Business Analysis", never "5 Years Business Analysis").

Link capability requirements to the exact profile capability name, eligibility requirements to the exact profile eligibility fact, and qualification requirements to the exact profile qualification name.
Use matched_candidate_fact for the matched profile fact and keep capability_name / eligibility_name aligned with the requirement_type.
Leave matched_candidate_fact empty only for not_shown or mismatch items.
Keep each requirement_coverage or eligibility_requirements item compact: short phrases only for requirement, matched_job_text, matched_candidate_fact, and profile_support.
Within requirement_coverage, prefer the most important atomic requirements when the ad is long. Never omit an explicit eligibility_requirements gate for this prioritisation.
Do not mark a requirement supported or partially_supported merely because the candidate has a broadly transferable capability. Transferability is not requirement evidence.
A supported or partially_supported match must prove at least one substantive element stated in the requirement itself. Return those exact job-requirement fragments in covered_requirement_elements.

If the profile only shows a broad parent capability but does not show the defining domain, technology, activity, qualification, methodology, or responsibility, use not_shown and leave matched_candidate_fact empty.

Examples of invalid partial matches: agile delivery does not prove investment appraisal or ROI; general business analysis does not prove banking experience; policy interpretation does not prove complaints, fraud, or case-management experience.

Set role_defining=true when a requirement or related group distinguishes the actual specialist nature of the role from generic duties of the occupation. Use the same short role_defining_group label for related specialist requirements. Do not mark routine generic duties as role-defining.
